tools.name: hacknotice_assessment_search
tools.title: Search Assessments
tools.description: POST /assessments/page across as many API pages as needed (50 rows/page) to return up to `limit` assessments in one call, with hasMore when more exist. Default limit 100, max 1000. Prefer this over hacknotice_assessment_list_assessments_page for broad questions across many vendors, e.g. "which vendors have an overdue assessment" (status: "overdue") or "which assessments score under 70" (scoreLessThanOrEqual: 69) — it removes the need to page through results or loop per company_id yourself. Still pass term when the user names one specific vendor.

debug.description: When true, include `_debug` with inbound MCP and outbound extension API request/response traces (secrets redacted). Set when the user prompt contains [debug].

term.description: Vendor or company name filter (case-insensitive). REQUIRED when the user names a specific vendor (e.g. "discover", "Acme Corp"). Sent as API body.term — matches assessment name and description.

companyId.description: Filter by company_id when known (e.g. from watchlist lookup).

sortBy.description: Sort field. Use timestamp (default) for latest assessment; score for highest/lowest scored.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction. Use desc for latest/highest score.

scoreExists.description: When true, return only assessments that have a score.

scoreLessThanOrEqual.description: Only return assessments with a score ≤ this value (inclusive). E.g. for "score less than 70" pass 69. Assessments with no score are always excluded.

scoreGreaterThanOrEqual.description: Only return assessments with a score ≥ this value (inclusive). Assessments with no score are always excluded.

requestBody.description: Optional extra API body fields merged after explicit filters (e.g. template_ids).

limit.description: Number of assessments to return, auto-paginating across API pages as needed. Omit for default 100. Max 1000. Response includes hasMore when more rows exist on the API.

tools.name: hacknotice_assessment_vendors_without_assessment
tools.title: Vendors Without Assessment
tools.description: POST /assessments/vendors-without-assessment. Returns watchlist vendors that have never had an assessment created at all (zero documents), answering "which vendors have never been sent an assessment" in one call — no need to fetch the full watchlist and assessment list and diff them yourself. Unpaginated; response is capped and includes `truncated: true` if the watchlist is larger than the cap.

debug.description: When true, include `_debug` with inbound MCP and outbound extension API request/response traces (secrets redacted). Set when the user prompt contains [debug].

active.description: When set, only consider watchlist items with this active flag.

tools.name: hacknotice_assessment_ai_score_unscored
tools.title: AI Score Unscored Assessments
tools.description: Loops POST /assessments/ai-score-bulk (small server-side batches) until either every eligible unscored assessment has been processed, `maxDocs` is reached, or a safety cap of iterations is hit — answering "AI-score any completed assessments that have not yet been scored" in one tool call instead of one call per assessment. Requires AI scoring enabled for the customer. Skipped assessments (e.g. unanswered questions) are reported but not retried within this call.

debug.description: When true, include `_debug` with inbound MCP and outbound extension API request/response traces (secrets redacted). Set when the user prompt contains [debug].

maxDocs.description: Stop once this many assessments have been AI-scored in this call. Default 100, max 500.

tools.name: hacknotice_third_party_watchlist_get_watchlist_domains
tools.title: Get Watchlist Domains
tools.description: POST /hackwatchlist/page across as many API pages as needed (50 rows/page) to return up to `limit` third-party watchlist vendors in one call, with hasMore when more exist. Default limit 100, max 1000 — omitting limit no longer requires you to page through the whole watchlist manually. Each returned vendor includes a computed `concernLevel` (low/medium/high/critical, derived from ransomwarethreatfactor: >15 critical, >5 high, >1 medium, else low — matches the Watchlist UI coloring). Use `sort: "ransomwarethreatfactor"` to surface the highest-risk vendors first, and `concernLevel` to keep only vendors at specific bucket(s), e.g. for "which vendors have a critical concern level".

sort.description: Sort order for third-party watchlist domains. alphadomain/alphaname sort alphabetically; threatfactor/ransomwarethreatfactor sort by that factor descending (highest risk first). DEFAULT (omit) = alphadomain, unless `concernLevel` is set, in which case it defaults to ransomwarethreatfactor.

concernLevel.description: Only return vendors whose computed Concern Level matches one of these values, e.g. ["critical"] for "vendors with a critical concern level". Filtering happens after fetching, on the same sorted window `limit` bounds — if `hasMore` is still true after filtering, raise `limit` to see more.

limit.description: Number of watchlist domains to return, auto-paginating across API pages as needed. Omit for default 100. Max 1000. Response includes hasMore when more rows exist on the API.

tools.name: search_global_breaches
tools.title: Search global breach incidents
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Search HackNotice's curated global breach database for published hack/ransomware/data-breach incidents by domain or company name.

USE WHEN: User asks about a ransomware attack, data breach, hack incident, or "what happened to {company/domain}"; needs published breach details plus HackNotice workflow next steps.

DO NOT USE WHEN: User wants forum/dark-web chatter (use search_chatter); structured leak/credential records (use search_exposure or search_credential_leaks); watchlist-specific alerts only (use hacknotice_third_party_alerts).

REQUIRES: Customer flag unlimitedthirdpartyaccess for search.

OUTPUT: breaches, watchlist status, recommendations.workflowActions (next steps you can run as tools) and recommendations.guidance (next steps the user must do in the HackNotice app; no tool exists for them). Both are empty when the search returns no breaches.

term.description: Domain or company name to search in the global breach database (e.g. destinlegal.com).

startDate.description: Optional ISO 8601 start bound on published_date (maps to start_date).

endDate.description: Optional ISO 8601 end bound on published_date (maps to end_date).

limit.description: Number of breach records to return (default 25; API returns up to 50 per page).

debug.description: When true, include `_debug` with inbound MCP and outbound extension API request/response traces (secrets redacted). Set when the user prompt contains [debug].

tools.title: Verify HackNotice credentials

tools.title: List saved searches
tools.description: Lists saved searches from the HackNotice API. Call this before alert tools when the user references a saved search by name or order (e.g. "first saved search"). Returns id, name, and savedSearchJson tokens for follow-up alert calls.

tools.name: hacknotice_third_party_alerts
tools.title: Third-party hack alerts
tools.description: POST /hackalerts/page with saved-search JSON, time range, and typed filters (sourcetype, sort, tier, tag, harvester, remediated, topNaicsCode(s), region(s), companyFilter, showUpdatedBreachOnly — the fields prod-api accepts on this endpoint). Returns up to `limit` alerts (default 100) with `hasMore` when additional API pages exist. Returns full, uncompacted records by default — pass compact or fields to shrink the response.

savedSearchJson.description: Saved-search token or JSON from hacknotice_list_saved_searches (same kind as the alert tool). When the user names a saved search, call list_saved_searches first, then pass savedSearchJson from one entry.

sourcetype.description: Filter by breach source type (maps to sourcetype).

sort.description: Sort order: alphabetically (by domain), timestamp, or severity. Defaults to published_date descending.

tier.description: Filter alerts by tier value (maps to tier).

tag.description: Filter alerts by tag name (maps to tag).

harvester.description: Filter by harvester/source name; matches either harvester or othersourcesharvester.

remediated.description: Filter by remediated status (maps to remediated).

topNaicsCode.description: Filter by a single NAICS industry code (maps to topnaicscode).

topNaicsCodes.description: Filter by multiple NAICS industry codes (maps to topnaicscodearray).

region.description: Filter by a single region (maps to region).

regions.description: Filter by multiple regions (maps to regionarray).

companyFilter.description: Case-insensitive substring match against company name, domain, or breach description (maps to company_filter). Applied to the fetched page only, after pagination.

showUpdatedBreachOnly.description: Only include alerts whose linked breach has a lastUpdatedDate (maps to showUpdatedBreachOnly). Applied to the fetched page only, after pagination.

timeRange.description: Preset time window (ignored when startDate or endDate is set). DEFAULT (omit this, startDate/endDate, and hoursAgo) = no time filter — first page of all-time results, most recent first. Only set a window when the user actually names one (e.g. "today", "this week", "since March"); do not add one just to narrow a broad or vague request.

startDate.description: Fixed bound (ISO 8601, e.g. 2024-06-01 or 2024-06-01T00:00:00Z). Extension API: hack/domain use start_date/end_date; research uses startdate/enddate.

endDate.description: Fixed bound (ISO 8601, e.g. 2024-06-01 or 2024-06-01T00:00:00Z). Extension API: hack/domain use start_date/end_date; research uses startdate/enddate.

hoursAgo.description: Rolling lookback (8–72 hours, maps to hours_ago). Use startDate/endDate for longer ranges. Overrides timeRange. DEFAULT (omit this, startDate/endDate, and timeRange) = no time filter — returns the first page of all-time results, most recent first.

limit.description: Number of results to return. Omit for default 25. Max 1000. Response includes hasMore when more rows exist on the API.

compact.description: Return a fixed summary shape (id, name, hit_value, timestamps, domain/email/ip, severity, sourcetype, passwordType, filename, remediated, matches) instead of the full record. DEFAULT (omit) = false — full records are returned. Set true to shrink large responses when you only need the summary fields.

fields.description: Return only these top-level field names from each alert record. Overrides `compact` when set — use this to trim heavy fields (like leak text) while keeping the specific ones you need.

debug.description: When true, include `_debug` with inbound MCP and outbound extension API request/response traces (secrets redacted). Set when the user prompt contains [debug].

tools.name: hacknotice_first_party_alerts
tools.title: First-party domain alerts
tools.description: POST /domainalerts/page with saved-search JSON, time range, and typed filters (redactPassword, infostealer, credentialDump, creds, passwordLength, passwordCriteria, aiflag, tag, tier, unmatchTier — the fields prod-api accepts on this endpoint). When the user asks for a saved search by name or position (e.g. "first saved search"), you MUST call hacknotice_list_saved_searches with kind firstParty first, then pass savedSearchJson from the chosen entry. Returns full, uncompacted alert records (including leakDoc blobs) by default — pass compact or fields to shrink the response, or lower limit if it gets too large. Default limit 25.

savedSearchJson.description: Saved-search token or JSON from hacknotice_list_saved_searches (same kind as the alert tool). When the user names a saved search, call list_saved_searches first, then pass savedSearchJson from one entry.

redactPassword.description: Mask password values in leak documents (maps to redact_password).

infostealer.description: Only include alerts flagged as infostealer log matches (maps to infostealer).

credentialDump.description: Only include alerts flagged as credential dumps (maps to credentialdump).

creds.description: Include extracted email/password credential fields in the response (maps to creds).

passwordLength.description: Minimum password length filter (maps to password_length).

aiflag.description: Marks the call as UI-driven to avoid re-triggering AI tagging on the returned alerts (maps to aiflag).

tag.description: Filter alerts by tag name (maps to tag).

tier.description: Filter alerts by tier value (maps to tier).

unmatchTier.description: When true with tier set, match alerts whose tier does NOT equal tier (tierattempted) instead of matching it (maps to unmatchTier).

timeRange.description: Preset time window (ignored when startDate or endDate is set). DEFAULT (omit this, startDate/endDate, and hoursAgo) = no time filter — first page of all-time results, most recent first. Only set a window when the user actually names one (e.g. "today", "this week", "since March"); do not add one just to narrow a broad or vague request.

startDate.description: Fixed bound (ISO 8601, e.g. 2024-06-01 or 2024-06-01T00:00:00Z). Extension API: hack/domain use start_date/end_date; research uses startdate/enddate.

tools.name: search_exposure
tools.title: Search structured leak records (not chatter)
tools.description:
PURPOSE: Search structured research leak records matching one indicator or keyword. This is NOT the chatter/forum search.

USE WHEN: User asks whether something appeared in leaked/breached DATA or structured leak records; single IP, email, domain, company name, or keyword; "any new alerts" or "anything in the last X hours" for a single term.

DO NOT USE WHEN: User says chatter, breach chatter, leak chatter, quick read on chatter, forum, dark web, posts, discussions, conversations, "what's out there", or "what people are saying" (use search_chatter). DO NOT use for credentials/passwords (use search_credential_leaks), files/filenames/extensions (use search_leaked_files), or multi-keyword co-occurrence (use search_correlated_leaks).

EXAMPLES: "Structured leak records for IP 10.107.200.4"; "Research leak data mentioning Acme Corp in the last week"; "Leak-record hits for user@company.com today".

OUTPUT: JSON with results (array), count, summary, hasMore, and limit; pagination is handled server-side.

startDate.description: Fixed bound (ISO 8601, e.g. 2024-06-01 or 2024-06-01T00:00:00Z). Extension API: hack/domain use start_date/end_date; research uses startdate/enddate.

endDate.description: Fixed bound (ISO 8601, e.g. 2024-06-01 or 2024-06-01T00:00:00Z). Extension API: hack/domain use start_date/end_date; research uses startdate/enddate.

Use 'match_phrase' when the user says 'exact match', 'match exactly', or 'match exact' (exact phrase, no wildcards). Use 'wildcard_pre' when the user says 'include prefix' / 'include prefixes', or 'match domain...' — matches text that ENDS with the term, i.e. any prefix is allowed before it (e.g., emails ending in @domain.com). Use 'wildcard_post' when the user says 'include suffix' / 'include suffixes' — matches text that STARTS with the term, i.e. any suffix is allowed after it.
